findings.F1: The book's short is not closed after Monday and Tuesday. Of 826,743 recorded bars, 70,135 carry a short outside the 48 hours after a Monday 00:00 bar, and none carry a long. Those out-of-window bars sum to a gain of -0.70, against +2.15 inside the window. Trades last a mean of 99 hours (median 48, maximum 2,833), and the leftover position most often sits on Wednesday (130 coin-windows).
findings.F2: Because of those overstays, the 1,586 trades average -1.22 % net (t -3.99, 28 % winners). This is against a mean short move of +0.90 % over the idea's own 48 hours on the 985 Monday cases (t 3.08).
findings.F3: The fall does not grow with the weekend gain; it shrinks as the forecast grows:
findings.F4: The fall grows with the coin's 30-day hourly volatility. By volatility quintile, the 48-hour short move is -0.81 % (t -0.99), +0.80 %, +0.90 %, +1.09 % and +1.79 % (t 2.19), about 155 cases each.
findings.F5: The effect rests on a few periods, which is why the leave-one-window-out Sharpe fails (-0.188):
findings.F6: Most of the fall comes on Tuesday. The short move is +0.18 % over the first 24 hours and +0.72 % over the second 24 hours (985 cases).
findings.F7: The fall is largest after a 30-day decline. It is +1.68 % (t 2.54) when the 30-day return is in its lowest quintile (-60 % to -21 %) and +1.31 % (t 2.27) in the next. It is -0.97 % (t -1.66) when the 30-day return is near flat (-4 % to +17 %).

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days (Monday and Tuesday), only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months; the higher the coin's 30-day hourly volatility at Monday 00:00, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the Monday fade by how turbulent the coin is, not by how far it rose over the weekend, and close it at the end of Tuesday.
ideas.name: turbulence-graded weekend rise reversal

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days (Monday and Tuesday), mostly over Tuesday, only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months; the higher that volatility, the larger Tuesday's fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade a weekend rise mainly across Tuesday in turbulent weeks, holding it no longer than to Wednesday 00:00 UTC.
ideas.name: Tuesday fade after weekend rise

ideas.idea: When a coin's price rises from Saturday 00:00 UTC to Monday 00:00 UTC, it falls over the following two days (Monday and Tuesday), only while the coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its own last 6 months and its 30-day return is negative; the deeper its 30-day fall, the larger the fall after the weekend rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade weekend rises in turbulent coins that are in a monthly decline, and do it more strongly the deeper that decline.
ideas.name: weekend rally fades in downtrends
